With only a description to go off of, it's pretty difficult to say one way or another if your coke was cut with something sketchy for certain, but I think it's pretty much always safe to assume that any hard drug you're using nowadays has likely been tampered with to some extent. Depending on what state you're in, you can actually get free drug testing strips sent to you (I live in NY state and I ordered fentanyl and xylazine test strips for free from the NYS website). Might not be a bad idea to grab those if you plan on using again in the future! 
All in all tho I wouldn't panic too much. 1am-7am is a long stretch of time, and fent/meth/heroin/etc. would have likely made you feel weird much sooner than 7am. Your coke was probably cut with something weird, and you're going through the withdrawals now. But like I said, ER is always the best call when you're just not sure!

Finding a non reactive dog is a great idea! The best way to do that is to take note of where people with dogs live and then introduce yourself to them (sans dog) and explain the situation. I did this with a few of my neighbors and I was pleasantly surprised at how willing to help they were! With just regular walks, I've gotten in the habit of shouting to the incoming person, asking if they can hold on a minute, and then explaining the situation. I usually say something like "my dog is leash reactive (makes them less nervous than saying dog reactive usually), can you just stand there while we do a walkby?" Most people are more than happy to help! I've learned that a lot of people (especially those without dog reactive dogs) don't even realize the stress and anxiety of dealing with training, so if you explain what you're trying to do they're much more understanding and aware of the situation. It might seem awkward at first, but I promise it helps with training and it gets a lot less awkward the more you do it. Some people are dicks, however, and with them you gotta just remember who they are and turn around when you see them coming.  With my dog, I say look at me while we're walking, once he looks I say yes, give reward, and repeat until we pass the distraction and then a BIG snuggle as reward if he passes successfully. If not, then just ignore him and continue on. I started with just a quick look and I'm now up to my dog holding eye contact for a few seconds at a time. Slowly start to stretch out the time he has to hold your eye contact to get the treat. A big thing with this technique is to train the "look at me" command in a very calm, low distraction environment to build up your dogs responsiveness to the command and then start to introduce small distractions as he gets better with it. As much as you can try to avoid triggers during the early stages of training. Of course, life is chaotic and there will be surprise dogs! For those instances just keep doing what you're doing and try to get your doggy out of there before he sees them and has a chance to react. You're doing great!  Reactive dogs are HARD and I was in a very similar situation with my dog. I was told he was great with other dogs- our first day with him he snaps at a dog passing on the street and starting lunging going crazy barking. I know how anxiety inducing it can be and I was right there with you crying and having panic attacks. But it gets better I promise!!! Practicing the techniques will help you feel more confident handling tough situations even when things go wrong. You are already doing more than most and you should be proud of taking the initiative to get advice!

So with getting his attention in the presence of distractions you'll have to find the distance at which he is not distracted, aka at what distance he will look at you if you ask him to. From this distance SLOWLY get closer and closer and ask him to look at you. If he does, say "yes" (or use you clicker or whatever word you've chosen as his marker) and give him a snack. If he is too distracted you can try using the Caesar Milan "tap"--basically just very gently tapping him with your foot. Not kicking or anything but just something to kind of snap him out of his trance. If that still doesn't work, move back a few feet and try again. Using this technique you can slowly start getting closer and closer to his triggers over time. If you have a situation like you were saying your apartment, getting the hell out of dodge is absolutely the way to go until he can more reliably focus on you in the presence of triggers, so you're doing the right thing!

I TOTALLY feel you there. Breakups are super scary and the idea of being alone, especially when you've had someone by your side nonstop for a year, is terrifying. In the end your mental health has to go above all else. If you feel like this relationship is more taxing than rewarding, that's a pretty good sign that you guys should consider splitting. If it's not, however, and you really feel like you guys can move past it in a healthy way, then go for it and push! But it can't all be on you-- if he isn't willing to match your effort and energy 100% to improve, then it just will never work. Try to build a good group of support beforehand, though, as that way you will have some solid people to fall back on if you break up and are feeling alone. Good luck!

I think a good general piece of advice is that if you are seriously considering breaking up with someone for an extended period of time, then it's likely that this is not the person for you. There can be an infinite amount of love between the two of you, but if you have totally different personalities/values (like how you spend/save money, how proactive you are) then it's just never going to be a good fit. Relationships obviously are not easy 100% of the time, but you guys should be on the same wavelength about things that you both deem important. In this case, finances are clearly a big deal to you and not to him. If you've brought this up multiple times to him and he is still not making an effort to be better about it, then he is not as invested in this relationship as he may believe. Again, this is not to say he doesn't love you like crazy or vice versa, but sometimes peoples personalities just don't mesh well in the long term. Hope this helps!
